research_concepts: design validity and power for personnel detection
methodological_questions: Does replacing a player in the offensive five change shot mix, measured from shot-distance and shot-type fields rather than derived play-type labels?
Can a within-game substitution design separate personnel effects from fatigue, score-state, timeout and shooter-selection confounds?
Does the design detect a known effect size (positive control) with adequate power before its null or positive result is interpreted?

historical_evidence.finding: Opponent lineup adaptation (shot mix when the opposing rim big is off floor), N=1.07M possessions. DRIVE +0.82pp (SE 0.25), POST_UP +0.43pp (SE 0.18), 3PA -1.79pp (SE 0.31), rim <=4ft +0.12pp (t=+0.4), PPP +0.008 (SE 0.007, t=+1.1). Recorded verdict WEAK/SMALL. This concerns the opponent's lineup, not the offensive five.

After-timeout shift in play-type mix: POST_UP +2.406 (t=+18.7), SPOT_UP +2.333 (t=+12.9), half-court PPP -0.0105 (SE 0.0056, t=-1.89). Method compared 56,423 ATO possessions with the same game-offense-period-minute. Shows that mix shifts after a stoppage can be measured, but it is descriptive and uses play-type labels.

Connector presence did not shield stars: dTS +0.05pp (p=0.937), dTO +0.74pp (p=0.00364, wrong sign). HasConn on-off PPP null (n=73). Lineup ORtg lift was a talent confound (p=0.51 after TALENT). Recorded failure mechanism B_powered_null.

Play-type label backfill verification failed: PNR 28.7% (band 20-28%), PULL_UP 7.9%, 2024-25 PULL_UP ~0-1% for many teams, team identity FAIL, 82.8% of PNR labels proxy_calibrated. Final recorded verdict FAIL. Recorded failure mechanism C_artifact.
PULL_UP exposure slope falls from -0.0255 (with lineup FE) to -0.0063 (no lineup FE); same-shooter placebo on other play types -0.0075. Recorded as consistent with a shooter-level confound.

Adaptation falsification tests (asymmetry, confidence gradient, carryover). Next-game PPP Welch t=-1.003, p=0.842. Recorded failure mechanism C_artifact, with selection/regression-to-the-mean limitation.

Defensive adaptation to repeated play type: league-wide within-game slope -0.0019 PPP/exposure (SE 0.0019); only PULL_UP survives Holm (-0.0243, holm p=0.0004). Recorded limitations include insufficient exposure and low measurement reliability.

Team heterogeneity in halftime play-type adaptation: heterogeneity variance not above null (p=0.363); split-half r=-0.026. Recorded failure mechanism A_unanswerable with team-season slope SD 0.6733 versus mean sampling SE 0.6508.
On-ball defensive scheme labels: 14.9% (DET) and 3.3% (ORL) of possessions labelled; switches_on unpopulated. Recorded verdict failed_gate.
Descriptive play-type mix shifts by halftime margin, crunch time and post-run; no inferential tests. OTHER label recorded as noisy. Failure mechanism E_unclear.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using backfilled, proxy-calibrated play-type labels (PNR, PULL_UP) as the mix outcome
failed_approaches.why: Labels failed band and team-identity checks; 2024-25 PULL_UP shares near 0-2% for many teams; 82.8% of PNR labels proxy_calibrated (recorded C_artifact).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Attributing a PULL_UP exposure effect to defensive adaptation without holding shooter and lineup fixed
failed_approaches.why: Effect shrank from -0.0255 to -0.0063 without lineup FE; placebo on other play types was of similar size, consistent with shooter-level confounding (recorded artifact_found).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating a within-game PPP lift after adaptation as a coverage response
failed_approaches.why: Wrong-way and no-signal comparisons did not match the adaptation hypothesis; next-game carryover null (p=0.842); recorded C_artifact with selection/regression-to-the-mean limitation.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labelling on-ball coverage from matchup fields
failed_approaches.why: Confident label rates 14.9% and 3.3%; switches_on not populated (recorded failed_gate, untestable).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Detecting team heterogeneity in adaptation with 120 team-seasons
failed_approaches.why: Team-season slope SD roughly equal to sampling SE; split-half r near zero (recorded A_unanswerable).

evidence_establishes: Shot-mix shifts of about 1-2pp in 3PA and drive/post share can be estimated at very large possession counts (FAM:SF34, SE 0.31pp for 3PA at N=1.07M), so the outcome is measurable in principle.
Play-type-derived labels from the 2024-25 backfill are not reliable enough to serve as the primary mix outcome (FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-APPS-058).
Within-game effects estimated without shooter or lineup controls can be produced by construction or confounding (FAM:SF-TMP-009, FAM:SF-APPA-001).
Lineup-composition comparisons are vulnerable to talent confounding (FAM:SF-APPS-087).
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests whether changing the offensive five moves shot mix. FAM:SF34 concerns the opponent's rim big and FAM:SF-APPS-087 concerns connector outcomes.
No retrieved record reports a positive-control or power calculation for detecting offensive-five personnel effects.
Nothing shows that a within-game substitution design can separate personnel effects from fatigue, score-state or coach-selection effects in this data.
The phrase 'showing the design can detect personnel effects' presupposes a non-null effect; no record establishes that such an effect exists.
own_inferences: The question is partly a validation claim. A positive shot-mix shift would not by itself show the design detects personnel effects unless the design also recovers a known positive control and the shift exceeds a placebo change.

Shot-distance and shot-type fields are probably more reliable outcomes than derived play-type labels, given the label failures recorded in FAM:SF-APPA-030 and FAM:SF-APPS-058. This is an inference from those records, not a tested result.
Substitutions are endogenous: coaches change lineups after runs, fouls, injuries and fatigue, so raw pre/post comparisons will be biased by the same events that drive shot selection.
Power for stint-level changes will be far below FAM:SF34's full-sample power. Any personnel effect near 1pp will probably be detectable only with many pooled changes and pre-specified windows.
uncertainties: Retrieval returned no record of an offensive-five substitution study, so the prior-work assessment rests on adjacent studies.
Sample sizes for specific five-man combinations and the number of usable substitution events are not recorded.
The data version and whether the NBA stats per-game files include the fields needed for shot location at each stint change are not confirmed by any record.
Predicted probabilities are judgement, not estimates derived from a record.

historical_effect.explanation: Retrieved records show that play-type labels have failed validation, that within-game adaptation effects often turn out to be artifacts, and that lineup comparisons are confounded. These changed the plan from an open test of 'does the five move shot mix' to a shot-distance-based, positive-control-validated design with placebo windows. They did not establish that the effect exists or can be detected.

blocking_constraints.text: Substitutions are chosen in response to score, fouls, fatigue and matchups, so raw shot-mix changes are confounded. Records FAM:SF-TMP-009 and FAM:SF-APPS-087 show this pattern in adjacent questions.
Lineup changes often follow poor stretches, so pre/post comparisons pick up regression to the mean, as in FAM:SF-APPA-001.
Stint-level changes are much smaller in number than full-sample possessions; power for a 1pp mix change is not established and must be simulated before any claim.
Play-type labels failed validation in FAM:SF-APPA-030; the outcome must use shot-distance and shot-type fields instead.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record answers whether changing the offensive five moves shot mix. Adjacent records cover opponent-lineup shot mix (inconclusive, small effects), after-timeout mix shifts (descriptive), connector lineup effects (null after talent control), and play-type label validity (failed). These establish the outcome is measurable at large N, the labels are not reliable, and lineup comparisons are confounded. They do not test the personnel question.

risks.text: Score state, foul trouble, timeouts, fatigue and opponent lineup may drive both substitutions and shot selection.
Substitutions following poor offensive stretches inflate apparent personnel effects through regression to the mean.
Stint-level effects may be too small to detect at useful power without pooling across many changes.
Specific five-man combinations appear rarely, leaving sparse exposure for combination-specific estimates.
Derived play-type labels failed validation; using them as outcomes risks spurious mix changes.
If shot categories are derived from play-type labels rather than shot-distance fields, the outcome inherits label error.
A design that detects a shift without a placebo and positive control cannot show it detects personnel effects.
Several shot-mix categories and windows increase the chance of a spurious significant shift.
Stint-level shot-mix shares are noisy; split-half reliability must be checked before use.
League shot-mix trends across 2022-23 to 2024-25 can confound season-level comparisons.

design.estimand: Within-offense change in shot mix (share of FGA by distance zone, 3PA share, rim share) when a pre-specified offensive five-man change occurs, relative to matched same-game, same-period windows with no five-man change. Positive control: a known shot-mix shift defined a priori as the benchmark. Validation claim: the design recovers the positive control and the personnel shift exceeds placebo.
design.unit: Offensive stint or possession window around a substitution that changes the five-man unit; one row per stint-change event, with the offense and game as clusters.
design.sample: NBA 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 regular seasons from play-by-play, substitution intervals and starters. Playoffs held out as replication. Use shot-distance and shot-type fields, not derived play-type labels or backfilled PULL_UP/PNR labels (per FAM:SF-APPA-030).
design.power: Before any run, simulate the minimum detectable shot-mix shift at the realistic number of stint-change events per pre-specified five-man change. Use FAM:SF34 (3PA SE 0.31pp at N=1.07M) as the scale reference only. Report the MDE; do not claim detection below it.
design.controls: Game, team and season fixed effects; period; score margin bucket; time remaining; minutes since last substitution (fatigue proxy); foul count; opponent defensive lineup and rim-big indicator; matched baseline windows from the same game-period-minute. Shooter identity held fixed where possible to avoid FAM:SF-TMP-009-type confounding.
design.falsification: (a) Placebo windows where the five is unchanged but other substitutions occur; (b) reverse-direction substitutions (removing a shooter vs adding one); (c) pre-period balance on shot mix before the change; (d) positive control recovery; (e) replication in playoffs.
design.multiplicity: Holm correction across the pre-specified shot-mix outcomes (3-4 categories). Pre-register the outcome list and the window length before the run.
design.decision_rule: Claim personnel effect only if (i) the positive control is recovered, (ii) the personnel shift exceeds the placebo shift at the pre-specified Holm-adjusted level, (iii) the effect holds in the playoff holdout, and (iv) the pre-period balance check passes. Otherwise report as uncertain or artifact, not as evidence the design can or cannot detect personnel effects.
design.data_version: NBA stats per-game files for 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 regular season and playoffs as of 2026-11-02, with the shot-distance and shot-type fields. Label-derived fields excluded from the primary outcome. Freeze the version and record it before analysis.

methodological_questions: Can changing the offensive five detect personnel effects on shot mix?
What confounders and selection effects threaten substitution-based lineup comparisons?
Is shot-mix change a valid outcome for detecting personnel effects?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

messages.content:
Research question (as posed on 2026-11-02, in the area of lineup and matchup effects):
Changing the offensive five itself moves shot mix, showing the design can detect personnel effects.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
